---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Long History Restatement Versus Booked Intangibles
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ebitda, ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5))), NEG(MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Going long high restated returns on intangible-inclusive capital and short high-margin firms whose intangible base is purchased and capitalized exploits both directions of the accounting distortion, and neither leg requires cash-flow-statement data.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen-5 two-leg construction delivered the archive's best alpha (8.2%, t 4.78) but sits on 0.078 coverage because both legs use oancf; here the long leg uses the ebitda restatement (alpha 4.3%, t 4.08 at 0.145 coverage) and the short leg uses the margin-times-booked-intangibles combination that produced a reliable -2.9% alpha. This tests whether the two-sided mispricing survives on triple the sample, which is the main robustness gap in the archive.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Industry Neutral Two Sided Intangible Signal
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5))), 3)), NEG(MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)))))
HYPOTHESIS: The two-sided intangible mispricing operates within industries, so neutralizing the long leg by industry should preserve the portfolio alpha while sharpening the cross-sectional slope.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen-5 combination has the best alpha but its FMB t-stat fell to 2.80, whereas the industry-neutral restated return alone had the higher slope (4.02); the likely cause is that the raw restatement ratio carries a static asset-light sector tilt that adds cross-sectional noise. This isolates that single design choice on the leading two-leg structure, addressing the disagreement between the cross-sectional and portfolio evidence.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Profitability Misclassification Gap
EXPRESSION: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(ib, at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Investors and standard profitability screens rank firms on reported earnings, so the mispricing is concentrated in firms whose restated intangible-inclusive return is far better than their reported return — the firms conventional accounting misclassifies as mediocre.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the sharpest expression of the economic story: the signal is the rank distance between economic and reported profitability, so it is zero for firms with no intangible distortion and large exactly where expensing hides productive capital. It also tests incremental content beyond the reported-profitability factor that FF5's RMW leg already spans, which the level-based restatement ratios cannot do.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Smoothed EBITDA Intangible Restatement
EXPRESSION: MA(RATIO(ADD(ebitda, ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5))), 3)
HYPOTHESIS: The restated return on intangible-inclusive capital is a persistent economic state, so a three-year average of the long-history version should be a cleaner sort variable than its single-year value while retaining full sample coverage.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Smoothing raised both alpha and t-alpha in the oancf restatement family (7.4% to 7.6%, t 4.03 to 4.26), and the ebitda variant is the only strong archive signal with coverage near 0.145, so combining the two established improvements is the natural consolidation step. If alpha rises toward the oancf versions, the earlier coverage penalty was pure measurement noise rather than a sample-period effect.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Validated Intangible Reinvestment Refined
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5))), 3)), IND_RANK(GROWTH(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that are expanding current intangible outlays while already earning a high restated return on total capital are reinvesting at high marginal returns, and the market recognizes this compounding only slowly.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen-5 reinvestment signal had the second-best FMB slope (4.55) but only 0.057 coverage because growth of a five-year rolling stock requires ten years of data; using growth of the current-year intangible flow preserves the economic content of expansion at far lower data cost. Smoothing the restated-return leg also stabilizes the conditioning variable that the interaction relies on.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Goodwill Accrual Overstatement
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Goodwill specifically records overpayment for acquired intangibles, so goodwill-heavy firms whose reported income exceeds operating cash flow have the least validated asset base and should underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The booked-intangible accrual trap produced a reliable -5.1% alpha but a flat FMB slope, and one plausible reason is that intan pools genuinely productive purchased technology together with goodwill; restricting the intangible leg to goodwill should make the short side economically cleaner and the slope more monotone. This isolates which component of capitalized intangibles carries the overstatement effect, a question the archive has repeatedly bumped into but never resolved.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
